newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ousted Afghan military chief confirms new fighting.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Afghan military chief confirms new fighting.

text.p: The Taleban militia is fighting forces allied with the ousted Afghan government along a new front in northwestern Afghanistan, a spokesman for the ousted military chief confirmed on Saturday.
The Islamic purist Taleban said on Friday they had captured the northwestern province of Bagdhis, one of six held by Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum.
"We have news of fighting in Bagdhis," the official spokesman for ousted military chief Ahmad Shah Masood said on Saturday. He could not confirm whether or not the province had fallen.
Dostum has allied his forces with those of Masood, who fled when the Taleban captured Kabul last month. The militia now holds more than two-thirds of the country.
The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) had quoted the Taleban governor in Herat province, Mullah Yar Mohammad, as saying his forces took control of Badghis after heavy fighting.
Taleban forces advanced into adjoining Dostum-held Faryab province and captured the southwestern district of Quaysar on Friday night, the AIP said.
The two provinces border Turkmenistan, which like other former Soviet Central Asian states have viewed events in Afghanistan with growing alarm.
Until Friday's report of fighting in the northwest, Masood and Taleban forces have clashed mainly on the plains north of Kabul.

Reuters correspondent Chris Bird said a Taleban plane flew a sortie over Jabal os-Siraj some 70 kms (44 miles) north of Kabul on Saturday morning, bringing scattered anti-aircraft fire. There was no word of casualties.
